title: runbook-sampler-daily-digest-nov09-2026
body:
Runbook sampler — daily digest (2026-11-09)

Attendees: Anika (notes), Miguel, Priya, Jonah, Yasmin (observability)
Location: perf-standup huddle / async notes
Context: small exploratory session to capture a reproducible short-sequence latency regression observed in the last two shadow runs (A/B pool). Goal was to get a concise capture, narrow hypotheses, and produce short-term mitigations for customer-facing lanes.

Summary of what we did
- Reran three focused scenarios on the morning shadow pool (pool-id: shadow-11-9):
  * short-seq chat (prompt+reply ~ 32 tokens) — bursty QPS profile (sine wave 0->250 qps)
  * mixed-seq (50/30/20 split short/medium/long) — steady 180 qps
  * kv-cache heavy (long conversation prefix reuse) — sustained 90 qps
- Environment: A100-80GB, runtime build: serving-runtime@v2026.11.07-rc3, model variant: open-llm-v2-quant-4 (kv-cache enabled), batching kernel: optimized-contiguous-v2
- Observed metrics (median of 3 runs each):
  * short-seq p50/p90/p99: 9.8ms / 42ms / 210ms  (baseline from 2026-11-02: 8.1ms / 34ms / 150ms) — ~18% up at p50, p90 up 23%, p99 up 40%
  * mixed-seq throughput stable, tail latency +15% at p95
  * kv-cache heavy: no notable regression vs baseline, p99 similar within 5%
- Side-effect: CPU steal on host during one short-seq run correlated with garbage-collected sidecar logs; trace ID 0x7a9c5e captured

Initial hypotheses (ranked)
1) Batching window drift: the continuous-batcher occasionally allowed a larger assembly window under bursty arrivals (increased from target 6ms -> 12ms) which amplified queueing for short sequences.
2) Kernel-path degradation: a recent micro-optim (contiguous-v2) seems to add overhead for very short sequences due to extra memcopy when KV cache is active.
3) Host-level interference: background log-archiver cronjob triggered on some hosts causing ephemeral CPU steal (observed once).
4) Scheduler warmup regression: routing policy for shadow pool now mixes dedicated and spot instances; spot warmup sometimes increases latency until ephemeral GPU warms caches.

What we captured (evidence)
- Traces: two full traces attached in linked_artifacts (slack thread) with per-span timings (batch-assemble, kernel-invoke, kv-lookup, response-serialize).
- Flame graphs: kernel-invoke for short-seq shows an extra memcopy + 0.8ms/row on contiguous-v2 path (PR #892 references this change).
- Batcher metrics: histogram of batch-assembly-time shows secondary mode at ~10-14ms during burst periods. Exported metrics to /tmp/run-captures/2026-11-09 (artifact saved in PR).

Quick repro steps (for bench team)
1) Checkout serving-runtime at v2026.11.07-rc3, ensure model variant open-llm-v2-quant-4 with kv-cache enabled.
2) Start local shadow pool using ci-shadow-config/shadow-11-9.yaml.
3) Run bench harness: tools/bench/run_micro.sh --scenario short-seq-burst --qps-pattern sine --duration 300 --capture-traces true
4) Collect traces: /var/tmp/bench-traces/*.span.json and upload to the slack thread above for tagging.

Short-term mitigations applied (today)
- Temporarily reduced continuous-batcher assembly window target from 10ms -> 4ms for shadow-11-9 via runtime feature-flag (flag: batcher.assembly_target_ms) — immediate p50 improved from 9.8ms -> 8.2ms in next run.
- Rolled back contiguous-v2 kernel for short-seq routing to contiguous-v1 for the shadow pool (config override). That reduced the observed extra memcopy span; p90 improved ~10%.
- Disabled log-archiver cron on two suspect hosts (ops ticket RINF-2147).

Longer-term work / hypotheses to validate
- PR #892 (kernel micro-optim) needs an additional codepath gate to avoid extra memcopy when kv-cache present for short sequences. Assigned to Miguel (GH review in progress).
- Batcher heuristic needs to consider arrival variance: add adaptive target that tightens under high CV (coefficient of variation) workloads — prototyping in branch batching-ctrl/adaptive. Owner: Priya. JIRA: RINF-2189.
- Add a lab test that runs extremely bursty short-seq patterns as part of presubmit smoke (to catch this regression early). Owner: Jonah. Ticket: RINF-2201.

Action items (owners + rough ETA)
- Miguel: land follow-up patch to PR #892 that gates memcopy; ETA 2026-11-12 (JIRA RINF-2178).
- Priya: prototype adaptive batcher heuristic + perf job for it; ETA 2026-11-19 (branch ready for bench runs).
- Jonah: add bursty-short-seq presubmit smoke + synthetic dataset; ETA 2026-11-16 (CI job id: ci-smoke-burst-43).
- Yasmin (observability): hook new batch-assembly histogram into per-route dashboard and add alert for secondary mode > 8ms; ETA 2026-11-11.
- Ops: complete host audit and ensure no production cronjobs on shadow pools; ETA 2026-11-10 (Ops ticket: RINF-2147).

Open questions / TODOs
- Is the memcopy unavoidable for contiguous-v2 on all GPUs or only certain driver/kernel combos? Need matrix testing on A100 vs H100 images.
- Should short-seq routing prefer contiguous-v1 by default until contiguous-v2 proves stable? (ops tradeoff: contiguous-v2 improved medium/long sequences).
- Can we embed a micro-benchmark for memcopy cost into kernel PR CI so regressions surface earlier?

Notes to self (informal)
- keep the short-seq runs in the daily night cadence for the next week; if p95 regresses > 20% trigger canary rollback plan.
- capture a lightweight replay kit for the customer-facing lane so SEs can reproduce on-demand.

Appendix (artifacts & quick links)
- Repro script: tools/bench/run_micro.sh (branch: batching-ctrl/adaptive)
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/892
- Ops ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RINF-2147
- Traces: slipped into slack thread above (search: "runbook sampler 11/09 traces")

End of digest. Will iterate on follow-ups in tomorrow's perf huddle.
